Question B-006-003-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Modern handheld transceivers commonly use a small threaded SMA connector for the removable antenna. Its size suits compact very-high-frequency (VHF) and ultra-high-frequency (UHF) radios.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "A PL-259 connector": A PL-259 is much larger and is associated with many HF station coax connections, not directly with most handheld antennas.
- sourceIndex 2: "An F-type connector": F-type connectors belong mostly to cable-TV style 75-ohm systems and are not the usual hand-held radio antenna fitting.
- sourceIndex 3: "An RCA connector": RCA connectors are common for audio or low-frequency accessory leads, not as the normal RF antenna connector on modern handhelds.
